# MedSync — Examination Shared-Parameter Registry (cross-exam QC)

**Status:** GATE A deliverable — **awaiting CSO (Fadhul) sign-off.** Generated by an exhaustive 9-module audit (vitals/triage · resus Disability · general · respiratory · CVS · abdominal · neuro · MSK · endocrine-vascular-foot) + clinical-identity reconciliation. This is a **living document** (grows as exams are added). It is the source-of-truth for the single-record-many-views sync to be built (GATE B+). See `examination-consistency-qc-kickoff.md` + ADR (proposed) 0073.

> **Principle:** each shared parameter is **ONE canonical record per encounter, surfaced in many views** — editing any view updates the one record; all views reflect it. This is shared identity, **not** field-to-field copying. It generalises the existing vitals carry-forward. Decision-support: sync reflects what the clinician recorded — it never invents, auto-confirms, or silently overwrites a finding, and **not-examined ≠ examined-elsewhere**.

**Audit result:** 125 candidate parameters · 107 appear in ≥2 modules (the registry proper) · 18 single-module candidates flagged to verify. **78 rows need an explicit CSO equivalence decision (⚑); 29 are unambiguous.**

## Sync rules by type

- **A (time-series):** any view records a timestamped reading; the _latest_ surfaces everywhere with provenance; history kept (feeds trend + monitoring). Different values over time = a **trend, not a conflict**. **GCS ≤8 → airway emergency must fire wherever GCS is set.**
- **B (static):** one record per encounter; a contradictory second value is **surfaced to the clinician to reconcile — never silently overwritten** (the QC win).
- **C (structured):** canonical with sub-structure (per side/site/group); a coarse _flag_ in one module is **fulfilled by** the detailed finding in another (e.g. general hep/splenomegaly flag ↔ abdominal structured liver/spleen; **the diabetic foot reuses the CNS sensory modalities — ONE canonical set**).
- **D (derived):** recomputed from canonical inputs; never separately entered (reuses existing vitals interpretation + foot-risk; **scores-0-≠-normal** preserved).

**Proposed schema (for review — no migration; section_data):** a per-encounter `canonicalParameters` store keyed by `canonicalId`, each holding `{ type, value | readings[] (Type A), provenance{module,clinician,atIso}, discrepancies[] }`; module fields become `field → canonicalId` bindings + a presentation. The reasoning engine reads the canonical value (counts a finding **once**).

## Reconciliation notes (borderline merges + possible misses)

Notable close-call parameters that appear in only ONE module and were deliberately NOT promoted to registry rows (each could plausibly be cross-module but the inventories show a single source): (1) etCO2 — resus-only capnography; would become Type A if respiratory/airway adopts it, flag for future. (2) Peak flow / PEFR — respiratory-only; a time-series candidate but not yet elsewhere. (3) ABPI / Buerger's test / acute-limb-ischaemia 6 Ps / rest pain — vascular-only; ABPI would be Type C per-side and Buerger's/6-Ps would surface in resus circulation if that module expands. (4) Murmurs (timing/location/radiation/intensity/pitch/manoeuvre), S1/S2, added heart sounds, apex beat (location/character/interspace/line), thrills, parasternal heave, pulse character/volume/rhythm — all CVS-only auscultation/palpation; genuinely single-module though pulse rhythm (AF) feeds the derived tachycardia/AF row. (5) Abdominal palpation core (rigidity, rebound, guarding, percussion tenderness, shifting dullness, fluid thrill, bowel sounds, masses object, Murphy's/Rovsing's/psoas/obturator/Courvoisier's signs, contour, distension 6Fs, hernias, stomas, surgical scars, Grey-Turner's/Cullen's, caput medusae) — abdominal-only. (6) MSK special tests (Phalen/Tinel/Finkelstein, epicondylitis, painful arc, rotator cuff, Schober, SLR, femoral stretch, Thomas, Trendelenburg, McMurray, Lachman/anterior-drawer, Simmonds-Thompson, etc.), GALS domains, distribution/symmetry/joint-size, morning stiffness, hot-swollen-joint, back-pain red-flag clusters (malignancy/infection/fracture/cord-compression) — MSK-only; the cord-compression and cauda-equina clusters DID cross into neuro and ARE in the registry. (7) Higher-cortical/speech/cranial-nerve singletons (orientation, attention, memory, frontal signs, neglect, dyspraxia, agnosia, Gerstmann, dysarthria, dysphonia, CN V/VIII/IX/X/XI/XII findings, optic atrophy, hypertensive retinopathy, RAPD, diplopia, ptosis) — neuro-only, though several relate to the focal-deficit composite. (8) Resus context booleans (opioidsSuspected, headInjury, alcoholMalnourished, pregnancyPostpartum, abcAbnormal, focalOnset/stroke-onset-time, seizureDurationMin, Cushing's triad, decorticate/decerebrate posturing, no-pulse) — resus-disability-only history/context flags; decorticate/decerebrate and Cushing's triad relate to GCS/raised-ICP but are not separately captured elsewhere. (9) Thyroid acropachy, thyroid functional status detail, ESRD/systemic-sepsis risk modifiers — endocrine-only. Borderline merges I chose NOT to make: 'malar rash (SLE)' vs 'malar flush (MS)' (kept as a CSO decision within one row, leaning separate); anaemia pallor vs ischaemic limb pallor (kept separate, flagged in the pallor row); pretibial myxoedema vs generic oedema (kept separate, flagged). Possible inventory misses worth confirming as future shared params: nystagmus (vestibular), peripheral cyanosis surfacing in CVS/vascular, spider naevi in general exam, capillary refill in resus C-step — all flagged 'verify' in their rows.
